bounded_additional_discoveries.finding: Qatar's incentive landscape actually comprises TWO distinct, currently-active programs, not one: the Doha Film Institute (DFI) Grants Program (competitive, non-recoupable, biannual -- qa_dfi_fund) and the NEW Qatar Screen Production Incentive (QSPI, launched Nov 2025, administered by a different body, the Qatar Film Committee at Media City Qatar -- qa_film_incentive). If CineGlobe's stored qa_film_incentive record reflects the OLD 30% DFI-administered rate, it is materially stale and superseded by QSPI's 40%+10% structure.

Two Lane C identities are DUPLICATES that should MERGE rather than remain separate canonical records: royal_film_commission_tourism_film_support merges into jo_rfc_rebate (Jordan -- no evidence of a separate tourism-film-support instrument distinct from the RFC cash rebate); sg_sfc_production merges into sg_imda_film_fund (Singapore -- the Singapore Film Commission is organizationally part of IMDA, not a separate incentive-granting body).

China's cn_film_incentive record, if it currently models a national rebate rate, is INCORRECT -- China has no national cash rebate/tax incentive for foreign productions; only city/regional-level rebates (e.g. Qingdao) and the CFCC official co-production pathway exist nationally.

acpfilms_fund.program_or_pathway: ACP Films — EU-ACP Cultural Film Co-production Fund
acpfilms_fund.starting_issue: Current competent-authority treaty text/list and administering program rule on co-production eligibility.
acpfilms_fund.authoritative_rule_set: ACP-EU Culture Programme audiovisual co-production support mechanism, financed by the EU's European Development Fund, managed by the ACP Secretariat. Grants allocated to existing co-production funds as additional funding. Applicants must be a consortium of >=2 organizations with equal/majority ACP representation. Grant range EUR 1,037,500-2,075,000, max 80% of total eligible costs. All formats/genres/lengths accepted (short, feature, TV series, web, documentary, VR, animation, video games).
acpfilms_fund.optimizer_consequence: STRUCTURE_PATHWAY_ONLY -- a competitive consortium grant, not a per-production deterministic rebate; not directly QPE/NPC-modeled the way a national rebate is.

cn_film_incentive.program_or_pathway: China Film Administration Domestic Co-production Support
cn_film_incentive.starting_issue: Current administering government/film authority or enabling instrument proving whether producer-accessible economics exist; if yes, official guidelines and statute/regulation.
cn_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: China has NO national cash rebate or tax incentive for foreign productions. International projects enter exclusively via the official co-production system administered by the China Film Co-Production Corporation (CFCC), or via location-only shoots under CFCC-facilitated permits. Sub-national incentives exist only at city/regional level (e.g. Qingdao: 40% cash rebate + 10% business-tax rebate, requiring >=50% of qualified spend at Dalian Wanda Studios, project cap RMB 120M) and are NOT a national program.
cn_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: cn_film_incentive as a NATIONAL existing-program record should be corrected to reflect NO national rebate exists; only the co-production pathway and isolated sub-national (Qingdao-type) rebates are real. If CineGlobe's stored record represents a national rate, it is INCORRECT and should be superseded by 'no national program; co-production pathway + regional exceptions only.'

eg_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: Egypt Film Commission (EFC), a subsidiary of Egyptian Media Production City (EMPC), offers a rebate of up to 30% on qualifying spend when productions shoot within EMPC premises and use EMPC facilities/equipment, plus additional relief of up to 20% on certain off-site expenses. Paid as a cashback against audited spend (not a tax credit). No automatic nationwide nation-wide nationwide tax rebate exists outside this EMPC-anchored structure. EFC now holds sole regulatory authority over all foreign production activity via a Single Digital Window (SDW) online platform (Egyptian Cabinet decision, late 2025).
eg_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: Rate/territoriality confirmed; EMPC-premises condition is a real, material qualification gate that should be encoded (rebate materially lower/absent off-premises beyond the 20% off-site relief).

gh_film_incentive.starting_issue: Current administering government/film authority or enabling instrument proving whether producer-accessible economics exist; if yes, official guidelines and statute/regulation.
gh_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: A 20% tax rebate for film productions plus import-duty/port-tax exemptions was ANNOUNCED by Ghana's government in February 2024 (State of the Nation address).
gh_film_incentive.effective_date: Announced February 2024; NOT confirmed as formally implemented as of 2026 per later sources, which state Ghana does not currently operate a formal national cash rebate programme comparable to European or island incentive models.
gh_film_incentive.remaining_issue: Whether the announced 20% rebate was ever formally enacted into law/regulation, or remains an unimplemented announcement, is genuinely unresolved from the sources available.
gh_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: Should NOT be priced as a live 20% deterministic rebate given credible later sourcing that it is not operative; closer to NO_CURRENT_PRODUCER_INCENTIVE_CONFIRMED than AUTHORITY_CLOSED, but flagged unresolved rather than forced given the direct conflict between the 2024 announcement and later non-implementation reporting.

hk_film_incentive.starting_issue: Current administering government/film authority or enabling instrument proving whether producer-accessible economics exist; if yes, official guidelines and statute/regulation.
hk_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: Create Hong Kong (CreateHK) was superseded by the Cultural and Creative Industries Development Agency (CCIDA) in June 2024, under the Culture, Sports and Tourism Bureau. CCIDA's current production-support activity (2026) consists of targeted scheme sponsorships (e.g. the Future Animation AI-Assisted Animation Production Support Scheme, up to HK$850,000 per company; the Asian Short Film Fund, up to US$35,000 per project) rather than a general percentage-based cash rebate for feature productions. The general feature-film cash incentive is administered separately by the Hong Kong Film Development Fund (see hk_film_dev_fund), not CreateHK/CCIDA.
hk_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: SUPERSEDED/CORRECT: CineGlobe's 'Create Hong Kong (CreateHK) Production Support' record should be renamed to CCIDA and re-scoped to targeted/scheme-based support, NOT confused with the general percentage rebate that belongs to hk_film_dev_fund.

hk_film_dev_fund.starting_issue: Current agency/fund guidelines, application call, award/recoupment terms, eligible-cost schedule, effective dates and source archive.
hk_film_dev_fund.authoritative_rule_set: Hong Kong Film Development Fund's Film Production Financing Scheme 2.0 (launched 15 January 2025, not time-limited) provides maximum financing of 40% of the approved production budget, capped at HK$10,000,000 (~US$1.28M), for productions with a budget not exceeding HK$25,000,000. 2026 enhancement: government funding disbursement upon commencement of principal photography increased from 50% to 70% of the approved amount.

ibermedia_programme.starting_issue: Current competent-authority treaty text/list and administering program rule on co-production eligibility.
ibermedia_programme.authoritative_rule_set: Programa IBERMEDIA, created November 1997 (Margarita, Venezuela Ibero-American Summit), operates under the Conference of Audiovisual and Cinematographic Authorities of Ibero-America (CAACI), coordinated via SEGIB. Currently ratified/financed by 18 member/observer states: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Chile, Ecuador, Spain, Guatemala, Mexico, Panama, Peru, Portugal, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic, Uruguay, Venezuela. Funded by member-state contributions plus loan repayments; supports co-production, distribution, exhibition, training and development via open annual calls to independent producers from member countries.
ibermedia_programme.effective_date: Current (2026 call cycle published on programaibermedia.com)
ibermedia_programme.remaining_issue: Per-call contribution minimums/maximums and recoupment terms for the specific 2026 co-production call were not itemized (the PDF bases document exists but was not opened line-by-line).
ibermedia_programme.optimizer_consequence: STRUCTURE_PATHWAY_ONLY -- membership/eligibility now confirmed for structure/candidate-generation purposes (which countries can route through Ibermedia); exact per-call financial terms remain a minor open item for a future pass, not blocking basic pathway modeling.

in_nfdc_coproduction.starting_issue: Current competent-authority treaty text/list and administering program rule on co-production eligibility.
in_nfdc_coproduction.authoritative_rule_set: India's Film Facilitation Office (FFO, under NFDC) administers a reimbursement incentive for OFFICIAL co-productions (bilateral treaty required) of up to 30% of Qualifying Expenditure in India, capped at INR 2 crore (~$240,000). Applies to co-productions granted official status on/after 1 April 2022. Incentive granted on recommendation of a Special Incentive Evaluation Committee. Separately, NFDC holds bilateral co-production treaties with 15+ countries enabling split-budget productions.
in_nfdc_coproduction.optimizer_consequence: This is a TREATY-CONDITIONAL incentive (requires official co-production status, not available to a purely foreign production without an Indian treaty partner) -- territoriality/eligibility gate should be encoded as treaty-dependent, not a blanket national rebate.

id_film_incentive.starting_issue: Current administering government/film authority or enabling instrument proving whether producer-accessible economics exist; if yes, official guidelines and statute/regulation.
id_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: Indonesia offers NO national incentive for foreign productions as of 2026. A Jakarta-specific (city-level, not national) tax rebate of up to 50% on Jakarta-incurred costs for QUALIFYING NATIONAL (not foreign) film productions was set to launch ~26 June 2026. A 1:1 matching grant from the National Cultural Endowment Fund is open to international co-production projects (a grant/matching-fund mechanism, not a rebate). Foreign shoots otherwise enter via Ministry of Culture permits only, with five city-level film commissions (Siak, Bandung, Yogyakarta, Bojonegoro, Banyuwangi) providing facilitation only.
id_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: No national deterministic rebate for foreign productions; only the co-production matching-grant mechanism and city-level (Jakarta, national-productions-only) rebate exist. Should NOT be priced as a national foreign-production rebate.

il_film_incentive.starting_issue: Current enabling regulation/decision plus administering-agency guidelines, QPE schedule, forms and audit/final-claim manual.
il_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: Israel's Fund for the Promotion of Foreign Productions (launched 2022) offers a rebate of up to 30% (capped at approximately NIS 16.6M / US$4.9M) on qualifying local spend, PLUS up to 10% for post-production and animation work. Competitive, round-based grant scheme with a fixed budget (not an open-ended statutory entitlement); applications made through an Israeli production company and assessed by an inter-ministerial committee.
il_film_incentive.effective_date: Program launched 2022; no confirmed sunset located
il_film_incentive.remaining_issue: CineGlobe's stored program name references 'Maslool' specifically -- this term was not corroborated in any source as the formal name of this fund; may be an internal/informal designation requiring verification against the Ministry of Culture and Sport's own Hebrew-language guidelines.
il_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: Rate/cap usable; note the fund is COMPETITIVE/ROUND-BASED with a fixed budget, not a guaranteed entitlement -- this should be modeled as CONDITIONAL/discretionary, not an automatic rate.

jo_rfc_rebate.program_or_pathway: Royal Film Commission Jordan — Production Rebate
jo_rfc_rebate.starting_issue: Current enabling regulation/decision plus administering-agency guidelines, QPE schedule, forms and audit/final-claim manual.
jo_rfc_rebate.authoritative_rule_set: Jordan's Royal Film Commission (RFC) cash-rebate program returns 25%-45% of qualifying LOCAL spend on a points-based system (project size, Jordanian cultural content, artistic/cultural/economic value); productions exceeding $10M with strong Jordanian cultural integration qualify for the maximum 45%. Minimum spend $250,000; capped at $5.25M per project (higher caps case-by-case). Up to 15% of post-production expenses for RFC-territory-performed services also eligible. Automatic exemption from Jordan's 16% VAT and 10% withholding tax adds effective total savings up to 56% of eligible spend. Local productions separately raised from 10% to 30% for spend >$500,000.
jo_rfc_rebate.effective_date: Rate increase to 45% announced May 2025, current through 2026
jo_rfc_rebate.optimizer_consequence: Rate is BAND-CEILING/discretionary (points-based, 25%-45%), not flat -- should be modeled as a floor(25%)/ceiling(45%) band with a discretionary uplift condition, matching the pattern already implemented for the MU/MT/GB pilot programs.

pk_pfc_rebate.starting_issue: Current enabling regulation/decision plus administering-agency guidelines, QPE schedule, forms and audit/final-claim manual.
pk_pfc_rebate.authoritative_rule_set: Pakistan's Film Policy 2018 (Ministry of Information, Broadcasting, National History & Literary Heritage) established: 10-year customs-duty/tariff exemption on imported film-production equipment (Finance Bill 2018 amendment to Customs Act 1969); a Film and Drama Finance Fund (FDFF) seeded with PKR 100 million (ECC-approved 15 Nov 2022) providing GRANTS (not a % rebate) to filmmakers; and a requirement that joint film/drama projects shoot 70% of the film in Pakistan to access these benefits.
pk_pfc_rebate.remaining_issue: No PERCENTAGE cash-rebate rate was located -- Pakistan's incentives appear to be duty exemptions + a grant fund, not a QPE-style rebate. ph_film_incentive.program_or_pathway: Film Development Council of the Philippines (FDCP) Incentive
ph_film_incentive.starting_issue: Current enabling regulation/decision plus administering-agency guidelines, QPE schedule, forms and audit/final-claim manual.
ph_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: Philippines' Film Development Council (FDCP), via its Film Philippines Office (FPO), operates THREE distinct programs: (1) Film Location Incentive Program (FLIP) -- 20% cash rebate up to PHP25,000,000 (~$450,000) for international projects engaging a Filipino company for line production/animation/post-production, with a 5% cultural bonus raising the total to PHP30,000,000 (~$540,000); (2) International Co-Production Fund (ICOF) -- up to PHP10,000,000 (~$180,000) for projects co-produced with the Philippines; (3) Film Location Engagement Desk (FLEX) -- facilitation only (permits/locations/logistics), not a monetary incentive.
ph_film_incentive.effective_date: Current (2025 cycle 1 confirmed active, ongoing into 2026)
ph_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: Rate/cap/cultural-uplift confirmed and usable; FLIP and ICOF are distinct programs and should be modeled as two separate segments/pathways, not merged.

qa_dfi_fund.starting_issue: Current agency/fund guidelines, application call, award/recoupment terms, eligible-cost schedule, effective dates and source archive.
qa_dfi_fund.authoritative_rule_set: Doha Film Institute (DFI) Grants Program is a biannual (Spring/Autumn) NON-RECOUPABLE grant program for development/production/post-production, supporting first- and second-time filmmakers worldwide and established MENA directors in post-production. Spring 2026 cycle: 48 projects funded across 39 countries (feature narratives, documentaries, shorts, TV/web series, experimental). This is a COMPETITIVE GRANT fund, administratively and financially DISTINCT from the Qatar Screen Production Incentive (QSPI) cash rebate -- see qa_film_incentive.
qa_dfi_fund.optimizer_consequence: STRUCTURE_PATHWAY_ONLY / FUND_GRANT_CONDITIONAL -- competitive, non-recoupable, not a deterministic QPE-style rebate; should not be priced as guaranteed incentive value.

qa_film_incentive.starting_issue: Current enabling regulation/decision plus administering-agency guidelines, QPE schedule, forms and audit/final-claim manual.
qa_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: SUPERSEDES the prior 30% Doha Film Institute-administered rebate. The Qatar Screen Production Incentive (QSPI), launched November 2025 (opening for applications Q2 2026) and administered by Qatar's Film Committee at Media City Qatar (a body distinct from DFI), offers up to 50% cash rebate on qualifying Qatari production expenditure: 40% base rebate + up to 10% uplift for hiring Qatari talent, local training investment, promoting Qatari culture, and other development criteria. Notably allows up to 25% of a project's total qualifying expenditure incurred in a SELECTED NEIGHBORING ARAB COUNTRY to also be rebated under the same programme.
qa_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: MATERIAL CORRECTION: if CineGlobe's stored record reflects the old 30% DFI-administered rate, it is STALE and must be updated to the new 40%+10% QSPI structure administered by a different body (Qatar Film Committee, not DFI). The cross-border 25% neighboring-country provision is a genuinely unusual territoriality feature worth flagging for careful modeling (not a standard single-jurisdiction QPE rule).

sa_sfc_rebate.authoritative_rule_set: Saudi Film Commission's cash rebate was RAISED to up to 60% of eligible expenditure (from a prior 40%), announced at Cannes Film Festival May 2026. Requires a registered/licensed Saudi production company OR an official co-production agreement with a local licensed partner, plus a No-Objection Certificate (NOC) for filming and proof of financial backing. Government/state-owned entities excluded. Covers production and post-production expenses only (pre-production excluded). Administered by the Saudi Film Commission.

kr_film_incentive.authoritative_rule_set: KOFIC (Korea Film Council) Location Incentive offers a 20% cash rebate on qualifying production expenditure for foreign productions, with an additional 5% uplift for projects shooting 10+ days AND spending over KRW 800,000,000 (~$613,500). Eligible: feature films, TV series, documentaries developed/produced by a foreign production company where foreign capital exceeds 80% of production cost. Now expanded to include Korea co-productions, not just wholly-foreign works. Refund processed within ~1.5 months of final settlement submission.
kr_film_incentive.effective_date: Current (expanded eligibility -- Korea co-productions -- effective from the cited program year)

kr_film_incentive.optimizer_consequence: Rate/uplift/eligibility usable with high confidence given source convergence; primary-source direct quote is a minor remaining polish item.

Funded by member-state contributions plus loan repayments; supports co-production, distribution, exhibition, training and development via open annual calls to independent producers from member countries.
